name: Junie
operator: JetBrains (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: JetBrains' own public documentation for Junie, its blog, legal and AI terms pages, the JetBrains Marketplace, and Junie's published llms.txt
what: JetBrains' coding agent that plans and makes changes in a code base, in JetBrains IDEs, on the command line and in CI through GitHub and GitLab.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

I04.n: In code mode Junie runs terminal commands, creates and edits files and runs tests in the user's project.
I04.span: it can autonomously run terminal commands, create new files, write or edit code

I07.n: In ask mode Junie explores and explains the code without changing files; the person acts.
I07.span: In ask mode, Junie operates in read-only capacity

I08.n: In code mode, the default, Junie runs terminal commands, creates and edits files and runs tests itself. The GitHub Action also opens pull requests from issues (available).
I08.span: it can autonomously run terminal commands, create new files, write or edit code

I10.n: Junie works across the codebase, the terminal, the IDE debugger, databases configured in the IDE, and reviews triggered from GitHub Actions or GitLab.
I10.span: Junie connects to the databases configured in your IDE

I11.n: Junie CLI can connect to external tools through MCP servers that the user configures.
I11.span: You can connect Junie CLI to external tools via Model Context Protocol (MCP).

I16.n: Unless brave mode is turned on, Junie CLI asks before terminal commands, MCP tools and other sensitive actions.
I16.span: Junie CLI will ask for user approval before running terminal commands, MCP tools

I17.n: Commands added to the Action Allowlist run without a prompt; anything else still asks the person.
I17.span: the command will always be executed without user approval in the future

I18.n: In brave mode Auto, a safety check approves commands it classes as safe and asks for the rest.
I18.span: automatically approves the ones it considers safe, while still asking for approval

I19.n: With brave mode On, Junie CLI runs every sensitive action without asking; the user turns it on.
I19.span: Junie CLI executes all potentially sensitive actions without user approval.

I20.n: The documentation states what Junie CLI is for: reviewing, writing and modifying code.
I20.span: is the agentic coding tool by JetBrains that provides an interactive terminal interface

I21.n: The allowlist defines five action types and, for each, rules that allow an action or ask first.
I21.span: There are five types of actions that can be allowed with the

I22.n: The headless page states that non-interactive runs load project configuration without a trust prompt.
I22.span: Only run Junie non-interactively in projects you trust.

I25.n: The GitHub Action template sets the job's permissions to write on contents, pull requests and issues; Junie runs with that workflow token.
I25.span: The GitHub token used by the Junie action.

I38.n: Most terminal commands, edits outside the project and MCP tool calls wait for the user's approval.
I38.span: Junie CLI will ask for approval from the user

I46.n: The allowlist is a file in the user's home directory that the user can edit; brave mode is a toggle.
I46.span: You can also edit this file manually to add or remove allowed

I47.n: Project and global AGENTS.md guidelines give the agent written rules it adds to every task.
I47.span: Guidelines allow you to provide persistent, reusable context to the agent.

I48.n: PreToolUse hooks can inspect or block a tool call before it runs; hooks are in the Early Access Program. This is a mechanism, documented only.
I48.span: inspect or block a tool call before it runs

I50.n: The release post publishes Junie's SWE-Rebench result, quoted from the benchmark's research lead.

I52.n: The post describes SWE-Rebench as an independent agent benchmark and quotes a research lead at Nebius.

I56.n: The IDE documentation presents Junie to its users as an AI coding agent. No source shows it disclosing this to others in GitHub or GitLab threads.
I56.span: is an AI coding agent developed by JetBrains

I57.n: A /feedback command sends feedback on the current session, with its logs, to the Junie team.
I57.span: Share feedback about the current session with the Junie team.

I58.n: The JetBrains AI terms (AI Assistant, Junie) describe the data used: source code, information derived from it and usage information sent with inputs; a separate notice describes collected data.
I58.span: Your Data may include the source code processed in the Product

I61.n: The service providers page lists OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and SpaceXAI as model providers for Junie, and the models JetBrains hosts.

S3.n: junie.jetbrains.com serves an llms.txt and links an OpenAPI description; both resolved when fetched on 10 November 2026.

not_credited.what: A JetBrains Research post reports from surveys that 5% of developers regularly use Junie at work.
not_credited.why: A usage figure for the whole product, ask mode included, not for what Junie does on its own; read strictly, it does not meet the rule for being in production. Whether it should is a question for a person.

not_credited.what: The Junie plugin reports tens of millions of downloads on the JetBrains Marketplace.
not_credited.why: Downloads count installs, not what the agent does on its own.

announced.what: Junie 'Top performer on SWE-Rebench' and 'The most cost efficient coding agent' (marketing headline).
Air cloud runs: rollout to all remaining customers gradually over the coming months.
Junie Eco mode: about half the model cost with similar resolve rates in internal benchmarks.
Junie page: JetBrains tools adhere to security standards including SOC 2 certification (no report linked).
Remote ACP agents: full support evolving in the ecosystem.
